title: 24 August 2006. Astronomers in Prague voted on what a planet is.
description:
Astronomers in Prague voted on what a planet is. The International Astronomical Union passed a definition at its General Assembly. Pluto was the casualty.

A planet must pass three tests. It orbits the Sun, it is nearly round, and it has cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit.

The first draft would have added planets. A proposal published on 16 August would have made Ceres, Charon and Eris planets, with twelve more candidates.

Open meetings killed it within a week. Members heavily defeated the Pluto-like object proposals on 22 August, and a new draft replaced it.

In favour of naming Pluto a dwarf planet, against 157.

Pluto became the prototype of a new category. Resolution 6A called it a dwarf planet and the prototype of trans-Neptunian objects.

Pluto did not change. The definition did.

Sources:
- https://www.iau.org/news/pressreleases/detail/iau0603/: read in full (IAU press release from the 2006 General Assembly closing ceremony, Prague Congress Center). Established the three criteria for a planet as worded in Resolution 5A; that Resolution 6A "passed with 237 votes in favour, 157 against and 17 abstentions"; that Pluto is a "dwarf planet" and "the prototype of a new category of trans-Neptunian objects"; and that 5A was not counted but passed with a great majority.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_definition_of_planet: read (first 39,403 of 70,213 characters verbatim). Established the final definition passed on 24 August 2006; 6A approved 237 to 157; the original proposal published 16 August that would have made Ceres, Charon and Eris planets with twelve further candidates; the open meetings of 22 August that heavily defeated the Pluto-like object proposals; and the rewritten third draft of 24 August that was passed.
